neighbours.label: a word-opening fragment spelling the 'sh' sound in non-English text, with the rest of the word still to come (French ' Ch'|ine, German ' versch'|wimmt, Russian ' ш'|пионов, Turkish ' ş'|ifre)

notes: Card: peaks are CJK byte pieces (15 of 32) plus ' Ch' (Chine), ' versch', ' ш', '-ch' (sur-le-champ), Arabic sheen, Turkish ' ş'. The Latin/Cyrillic/Arabic ones all spell /sh/ at a word start that the tokenizer split. Probes: 'en Chine' 0.72, ' ш' 0.60, ' versch' 0.34, Japanese 0.36; 'en France' 0.03, English 'China' 0.00. The label does not explain the CJK examples. Near misses are the same languages with split words that have no /sh/ (' verst'|ehen, ' кни'|га, ' kit'|ap). Tokenizer splits were checked beforehand (no scoring).
